The `source` array downloads a tarball from the package's own GitHub releases URL (`https://github.com/Govcraft/acton-ai/releases/download/v0.35.0/acton-ai-0.35.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz`), which is the project's upstream source. The `sha256sums` is set to a specific hash (not `SKIP`), so the downloaded archive will be verified during extraction. There is no `pkgver()` function — the version is declared directly as `0.35.0`. The top-level scope and any potential `pkgver()` contain only variable assignments, with no code that downloads and executes untrodied payloads, uses `eval`/`base64`/`curl|bash`, or exfiltrates data. The `package()` function (which is not run during this gate) simply installs the bundled binary to `$pkgdir/usr/bin/acton-ai`. No network requests beyond the expected source download, no obfuscated commands, and no unexpected file operations are present in the code that runs during fetching/parsing.
</details>
